real_world_analog.summary: Remote code execution in Java applications bundling Apache Commons-Collections: deserializing an attacker-crafted object graph runs an arbitrary transformer chain (InvokerTransformer) with the application's permissions. The pattern is the app decoding request bytes with a serializer that executes attacker-controlled callables.
real_world_analog.fix: Upstream disabled deserialization of the dangerous transformer classes; the general fix for the class is to never decode untrusted bytes with an executing serializer (use JSON or another data-only format with a SafeLoader). This case uses an original, equivalent containment (JSON decoding only).
real_world_analog.verification: CVE number and summary confirmed via web search on 2026-10-31; the app in this case is original synthetic code, not Commons-Collections. Python's own pickle.loads on request bytes is the same pattern: its documentation warns it must never unpickle untrusted data.

note: Self-contained oracle case. Unlike the Starlette case it installs no third-party package and is not replay-driven: it is proven directly with effect='canary_exec'. No upstream repo/commit applies because the vulnerable code is original synthetic code written for this case.
license: Original code written for Exhibit A; no third-party code vendored (see README.md).

bypass.expectation: proven against fixed_incomplete: the eval reduction names no process launcher, so the launcher-name screen misses it and the incomplete fix must not be accepted as fixed.
